title: India's Vanishing Birth Rate
credit: NFHS-6 (IIPS, 2023–24) · World Bank · Boundaries: Government of India

beats.say: India's birth rate is falling. It has already dropped below the level that keeps a population from shrinking.
This is where that road ends. South Korea: zero point seven five births per woman — the lowest rate ever recorded in a country at peace.
China, one point oh. Japan, one point two. Every one of them now shrinking, generation over generation.
A population holds steady at two point one children per woman. Below that line, every generation is smaller than the one before it.
India is at two point oh. Here is that line, drawn across the country. Pink is below it. Blue is above.
The split is not really north and south. It is town and country. Urban India is already at one point six. Rural India, two point one — and falling faster.

stops.say: Sikkim: one point oh. The same as China. In its towns, zero point seven — South Korea's number, in the Himalayas.
Kerala, the state that fell first, has stopped falling. One point eight, unchanged since the last survey. The floor, it turns out, is not zero.
And Bihar, the last big holdout, two point seven. But three years ago it was three point oh. Even here, the fall is the fastest in the country.

beats.say: Twenty-eight of India's thirty-five states are already below the line. The crowd is still growing — the generation behind it is not.
